title: Co-Evolving LLMs and Embedding Models via Density-Guided Preference Optimization for Text Clustering
subcategory: bidirectional LLM-embedder co-training (preference optimisation + contrastive learning)
task: Text clustering across topic, emotion, type, domain and intent discovery
problem: Existing LLM-assisted clustering treats LLMs as static pseudo-oracles or augmenters and never transfers dataset-specific distribution knowledge back into the LLM.
architecture: DG-CoE: task-aware prompts make the LLM generate interpretations of each text; interpretations are embedded and those in high-density regions are chosen as preferred samples for preference optimisation of the LLM; the embedding model is trained contrastively (plus DEC loss) on the interpretations; iterated co-training, k-means for final clusters.
key_results: Average over 14 datasets after two iterations: ACC 55.14 / NMI 66.31 vs 52.69 / 64.90 for Keyphrase and 50.64 / 63.45 for ClusterLLM.
strengths: First to fine-tune the LLM with feedback from the embedding model's density.
Baselines re-run with the same open LLM for a fair comparison.

limitations.text: Requires the number of clusters to be known.
LLM is used in training and inference, adding cost.
Preferred interpretations can be low-confidence and degrade results on some datasets (e.g. Bank77 with Qwen).
